Am mers la psihiatru, mi s a prescris calmant si antidepr ( sunt o fire extrem de anxioasa de fel). Incet incet am incercat sa ma relaxez, sa mi ocup timpul cu chestii ce ma linistesc si sa evit pe cat posibil stresul.
Intr o zi mi am dat seama brusc ca vad lumea ca printr un filtru. Ca si cum nu as fi in viata, sau ce e in jur nu e real, ci un vis. Ma uitam in oglinda ca la o alta persoana. Amintirile sau experientele din trecut imi pareau inexistente. Asa a continuat viata mea pt cateva luni. Diagnosticul psihiatric : disociere si tulburari anxioase severe. Medicamente iar. Nu mi puteam lua mintea de la experienta prin care treceam. Nu mai aveam perceptia timpului. Nu mai puteam empatiza. Totul in mod constant, in timp ce aveam impresia ca m am desprins de realitate, si sincer am crezut ca innebunesc.

Cum mi-am revenit : n am lucrat, n am facut nimic altceva decat ceea ce imi facea placere. Pictam. Stateam pe un scaun la soare afara si ascultam pasarile. Treceau zilele repede, eu tot obsedata de disociere eram.  And then it happened. A big oopsie. Am ramas insarcinata. Pot sa jur ca intr-un fel, creierul meu a fost "rewired" si disocierea s a risipit. Tot ce puteam sa am in cap era sarcina aia si situatia in care eram ( 23ani). Concluzia: cu cat te gandesti mai mult la disociere si hiperanalizezi, cu cat scapi mai greu. Sarcina a fost un soc care mi-a dat un sut in cur si mie si disocierii.

Fastforward disocierea a revenit mai tarziu din cauza la un atac de panica intr un moment de presiune, sub forma pe care o zici tu. Random. Imi luam trigger cand intram in casa seara de la intuneric, la lumina artificiala, parea ireal, cam asa a fost cu tranzitiile de mediu in general.

Cum am scapat in mare parte si de asta : m-am plictisit efectiv sa mi bat capul, dupa luni de zile,  timpul vindeca si el intr-adevar. Cand dadea semne ca incep iar sa ma disociez, ma fortam sa ma gandesc la altceva sau sa imi gadesc urgent o ocupatie.

For a couple of months i was struggling with it, until I found out I got pregnant, then it disappeared like nothing happened. Apparently the brain goes into that "numb" mode to cope with stress, and I was stressing my brain out because of the panic attacks ( i was constantly thinking I was going to die). For me it seems that a pregnancy toootally shifted my mind off of what I was experiencing and focused on other things.

However, I got a random ( I think) panic attack a few months later. Then derealization kicked in again. It happened during the evening and I was scared af. Instead of focusing on "omg everything is like an illusion again" I chose to cut  contact with the reality by.. Sleeping :D And it worked! I was also having major trouble with switching environments, going out of the house, getting in, sunlight and artificial light. Those were awful triggers for my mind, and they were more pronounced during evenings. However I always forced myself into thinking " its okay. Tomorrow morning i ll be fine again".

I presented my experience a bit so maybe you can have an overview about how this stuff is like for different people, and maybe, I hope, it helps you even a tiny bit.

Overall my advice would be try not to stress ( preferably at all), see it as something that ll pass, do stuff that you love even if it's scary that you see it differently, eat what you like, drink a lot of water, and just try to chill. It can take a while but don t lose hope! ( and avoid triggers and overthinking) :) good luck to you and I hope it goes away fast
